document.title: br-ai-nstorm — Project Update
document.purpose: Capture the latest conceptual and implementation shift of br-ai-nstorm as a structured project-memory update: what changed, what became clearer, what was built, what was dropped or deferred, and what remains unresolved.

project_identity.visible_product_frame: A living map of collective problem solving.
project_identity.deeper_research_frame: A practical wrapper for testing Open Cognitive Bubbles: independently controlled AI-extended thinking environments contributing bounded, interoperable objects to a shared problem space.
project_identity.current_north_star: One eyesight should tell a participant where the collective thinking currently stands, what changed, what happened to their own contributions, and what might be useful to think about next.

where_the_idea_started.initial_form: ATProto-inspired application-independent data plus Delta.dev-style checkout semantics.
where_the_idea_started.early_thesis: The app should not own the canonical data. Interfaces should be temporary views or checkouts over durable shared state.
where_the_idea_started.later_reframe: The persistent object became collective/project memory, with threads as collaborative workspaces and LLM compute helping reconstruct relevant context.
where_the_idea_started.next_reframe: The strongest interaction was identified as multiple people having personal AI conversations that draw from and contribute to shared, permissioned collective memory.
where_the_idea_started.current_reframe: The concept moved from project memory to Open Cognitive Bubbles: independently controlled AI-extended cognition connects to a shared problem through governed apertures.

major_shift_1_product_wrapper.before: The concept was mostly explained as collective memory, checkout, semantic commit, dynamic UI, and distributed cognition.
major_shift_1_product_wrapper.now: The visible product is intentionally much simpler: a collaborative brainstorm/problem-solving app.
major_shift_1_product_wrapper.reason: The deeper architecture is too abstract to validate directly. br-ai-nstorm provides a concrete UX where the hidden architecture can be tested.

major_shift_2_problem_not_project.before: A project or organization was treated as the persistent object.
major_shift_2_problem_not_project.now: A problem is the primary visible object.
major_shift_2_problem_not_project.reason: Problems are more flexible than projects and make cross-institutional, community, research, and city-scale collaboration possible without forcing one organizational boundary.

major_shift_3_state_not_map.before: The D3 relationship map was close to becoming the primary representation.
major_shift_3_state_not_map.now: Canonical semantic state is primary; Map and Timeline are synchronized views.
major_shift_3_state_not_map.reason: Force-directed position is not a stable ontology. Users need a clear canonical structure they can understand immediately.

major_shift_4_one_eyesight_view.before: The interface emphasized exploration through a network map.
major_shift_4_one_eyesight_view.now: The interface must answer at a glance: Where are we now? What changed? What happened to my thinking? What is still unresolved? What should I think about next?
major_shift_4_one_eyesight_view.reason: This is the strongest human-facing value proposition discovered so far.

major_shift_5_clipboard_as_fake_protocol.before: Interoperability was discussed in terms of future ATProto, APIs, MCP, federation, or agents.
major_shift_5_clipboard_as_fake_protocol.now: Interoperability is simulated with a clipboard JSON round-trip.
major_shift_5_clipboard_as_fake_protocol.reason: This isolates the real hypothesis without infrastructure distractions.

major_shift_6_lexicon_like_contract.before: ATProto was mostly an architectural inspiration.
major_shift_6_lexicon_like_contract.now: ATProto-style Lexicon thinking becomes useful as an interchange schema between br-ai-nstorm and arbitrary external LLM environments.
major_shift_6_lexicon_like_contract.reason: The system does not need to standardize the internal cognition process; it only needs to standardize what crosses the boundary.

major_shift_7_hidden_private_reasoning.before: There was concern that the individual reasoning process is hidden from the collective.
major_shift_7_hidden_private_reasoning.now: This is accepted as an intentional first participation mode: private reasoning stays private; only bounded reviewed contributions enter shared memory.
major_shift_7_hidden_private_reasoning.reason: The private process is not automatically the shared artifact. This mirrors the aperture model.

problem.definition: The shared question or challenge the group is working on.
problem.role: Persistent visible anchor for the collective state.

contribution.definition: Anything a participant adds that changes or enriches the problem state.
contribution.ux_principle: Participants should not need to classify before thinking. Classification can be proposed after the contribution exists.

orchestration.definition: AI-mediated context coordination around the problem.
visible_behaviors: what I might usefully think about next
orchestration.important_distinction: The AI orchestrates context, not people.

evaluation.definition: The changing epistemic state of contributions and solution directions.
evaluation.important_distinction: This is not likes or social popularity. It is intended to communicate problem-solving state.

canonical_information_architecture.principle: The semantic categories are canonical. Visual layouts are projections over the same state.

map.purpose: Explore relationships, clusters, support, contradiction, and emerging structure.
map.warning: Position is exploratory and must not imply canonical hierarchy or truth.

timeline.purpose: Show the diachronic evolution of the problem state.

since_you_were_here.purpose: Summarize how the collective state changed since the participant last engaged.

your_traces.purpose: Show what happened to the participant's previous contributions.
examples: became part of an emerging approach
your_traces.important_ux_insight: The system should show not only what people posted, but what their contributions did to the shared thinking.

think_next.purpose: Provide participant-specific prompts based on gaps, prior contributions, expertise, and current problem state.
think_next.important_ux_insight: This is where orchestration becomes personally useful instead of becoming a generic AI summary.

flow: Participant opens a problem in br-ai-nstorm.
Participant chooses 'Think with my AI' or 'Think privately'.
br-ai-nstorm exports a structured context package.
Participant pastes it into ChatGPT, Claude, Mistral, Gemini, a local model, or another LLM.
The external LLM returns only a bounded contribution package.
Participant pastes the JSON back into br-ai-nstorm.
The app validates the schema and enriches shared problem state.

aperture_and_interoperability.important_theoretical_move: Do not standardize the internal cognitive process. Standardize the contribution boundary.

previous_prototype.lesson: The interaction model felt compelling, but the map needed to be demoted from canonical representation.

latest_build.key_design_decision: Canonical state first. Map and Timeline are synchronized derived views.

what_is_now_deferred.reason: Too early before validating the visible interaction.
Schema thinking is useful now; federation is not required yet.
Event-style thinking may matter later, but the prototype does not need infrastructure complexity.
The current graph can be represented in normal application state or relational storage.
Canonical information architecture must become stable before adding situational UI generation.
Tasks, Kanban, timelines, and delivery workflows would dilute the core collective-problem-solving hypothesis.
Plurality, disagreement, provenance, and uncertainty are intentional parts of the model.

what_is_new_and_promising: A problem state that persists independently of any one AI conversation.
Participants can use arbitrary external LLMs through a common interchange schema.
The private reasoning process can remain private while bounded outputs become interoperable.
The system shows what a contribution did to collective thinking, not just that it was posted.
AI orchestration can personalize what changed and what a participant should think about next.
The map is repositioned as one exploratory projection rather than the truth model.
The product wrapper provides a practical way to test the Open Cognitive Bubbles hypothesis without exposing the deeper architecture to users.

product: Is br-ai-nstorm best understood as brainstorming, communal problem solving, collaborative sensemaking, or something else?
What problem type produces the strongest 'this is better than a shared chat' moment?
Does one-eyesight problem state become valuable enough to create repeat use?
ux: What is the clearest canonical structure for first-time users?
How many semantic categories can users understand without explanation?
Should the default State view be cards, columns, a structured canvas, or another layout?
How should evaluation status be shown without turning the system into voting?
How much provenance should be visible by default?
orchestration: What should AI surface automatically versus only on request?
How can 'think next' prompts feel insightful rather than annoying?
How can the system avoid reinforcing the loudest or most active contributors?
How should unresolved minority positions remain visible?
interoperability: Can multiple external LLMs reliably consume the same context package and return valid interoperable contributions?
How much system prompt and shared state is necessary in the exported package?
Should the context package be a record, a message envelope, or both?
When does formal ATProto Lexicon work become justified?
privacy: When private drafts become richer, what exactly may the exported context reveal?
Can future similarity/overlap detection be useful without becoming surveillance-like?
What participant controls are understandable enough to become real aperture permissions?

next_iteration_plan.goal: Make the canonical State view clearer and more compelling while preserving Map and Timeline as optional synchronized projections.

priority_1.name: Canonical state model
tasks: Refine semantic categories.
Define evaluation/status vocabulary.
Make current solution state understandable in one eyesight.
Clarify open, supported, disputed, untested, and emerging states.

priority_2.name: Contribution lifecycle
tasks: Show original contribution.
Show provenance.
Show later links and reactions.
Show current role in the problem.
Support superseded/contradicted/merged relationships without deleting history.

priority_3.name: Clipboard interoperability test
tasks: Test the same exported context with several LLMs.
Measure schema compliance.
Compare the quality and diversity of returned contributions.
Refine the contextPackage and contributionPackage schemas.

priority_4.name: Evaluation
tasks: Add contribution-level epistemic statuses.
Avoid popularity metrics.
Test whether status changes make the collective state easier to interpret.

priority_5.name: Real collaborative test
tasks: Choose one bounded real problem.
Use 3-6 people.
Let participants use different LLMs.
Track whether the shared state surfaces useful thinking that would otherwise disappear.
Compare with ordinary shared chat.

priority_6.name: Future City2Graph connection
tasks: Treat City2Graph output as evidence/context for city problems.
Allow a spatial projection to become another derived view.
Do not mix geographic truth with semantic problem-state layout.
Test Basel heat stress as the first linked case.

current_hypothesis_to_falsify.statement: A group solving a problem gains value when individual participants can take a canonical shared problem state into their own AI environment and return bounded interoperable contributions, while the shared system continuously shows how the collective understanding is changing.
success_signals: Participants understand the current problem state faster than through shared chat history.
Participants see useful effects of their own contributions.
Different external LLMs can contribute through the same schema.
The system surfaces useful unresolved questions or connections.
Returned contributions improve the shared state rather than create noise.
failure_signals: The State view becomes more confusing than chat or a normal whiteboard.
Users do not care what happened to earlier contributions.
External LLM outputs require too much cleanup.
The D3 map looks impressive but contributes little to understanding.
A normal shared chat plus summary performs just as well.

current_best_summary.short: br-ai-nstorm is becoming a canonical shared problem state with personal AI apertures, not simply a collaborative mind map.
current_best_summary.long: The latest iteration turns the Open Cognitive Bubbles research idea into a concrete collaborative problem-solving product. A group works around a persistent semantic problem state. Participants can see what changed, what happened to their own contributions, what remains unresolved, and what they might usefully think about next. State is canonical; map and timeline are projections. The first interoperability layer is intentionally primitive: the app exports a Lexicon-like JSON context package into any external LLM, private thinking happens there, and only a bounded structured contribution is copied back. This tests the central hypothesis before building federation, APIs, ATProto infrastructure, or autonomous agents.
current_best_summary.ironic_meta_note: This update itself is the kind of object br-ai-nstorm should eventually generate automatically: what changed, where the concept moved, what became central, what was deferred, and what remains to think about.
